name: PERIPHERAL BLOOD FOR HIGH RESOLUTION KARYOTYPING (SINGLE)

data.value:
Sample Type                       : Peripheral Blood
Clinical Indication : Down’s phenotype
Culture Type : 72 Hrs PHA Stimulated
Medium : RPMI 1640
Banding Technique : GTG
Banding Resolution : 400-550
Metaphases Counted : 10, low index
Metaphases Analysed : 10
Metaphase karyotyped : 05
   
RESULT  
Karyotype : 47,XY,+21
Diagnosis : Abnormal Male karyotype consistent with Down syndrome


Interpretation:
An abnormal male chromosome complement with an additional chromosome 21 was observed in all metaphases. This result is consistent with the clinical diagnosis of Down Syndrome.

Down Syndrome occurs when an individual has a full or partial extra copy of chromosome 21. There are three types of Down syndrome: trisomy 21 (nondisjunction) accounts for 95% of cases, translocation accounts for about 4% and mosaicism accounts for about 1%.

Early treatment programs can help improve skills. They may include speech, physical, occupational, and/or educational therapy. With support and treatment, many people with Down syndrome live happy, productive lives (http://www.ndss.org/Down-Syndrome/Down-Syndrome-Facts/; NIH: National Institute of Child Health and Human Development).

After the diagnosis of a child with trisomy, the recurrence risk for future pregnancies is about 1% when the mother is under 30 years of age. For women who are over 30 years old, the risk is based on age.

Note: The following possibilities, although rare, cannot be rule out:
a) Low level mosaicism and microdeletion
b) Very subtle rearrangement
c) Genetic disorder
 
Advise: Genetic counseling and Prenatal diagnosis should be recommended for all future pregnancies.
